__comment: Per-site login recipes — EXAMPLE. Copy to the path in LOGIN_RECIPES_FILE
(default ~/.config/rssfeed/login-recipes.json) and fill in your own sites.
WHY THIS ISN'T IN THE REPO
The set of sites you can log into is the set of subscriptions you pay for.
That's data about you — on a public repo it advertises what you read and
subscribe to. So it's configuration, kept outside the tree, like your .env.
WHEN YOU NEED ONE
Usually never: without a recipe the login uses generic heuristics
(input[type=email], input[type=password], button[type=submit]) that work on
most plain login forms. Add a recipe only when those misfire — typically an
ad-heavy page with several submit buttons where the generic selector clicks
the wrong one. Find the real selectors in devtools; a failed login leaves a
screenshot in /tmp/rssfeed-login-debug to help.
FIELDS
login_url           required — the page carrying the login form
username_selectors  optional — tried in order; first visible match wins
password_selectors  optional
submit_selectors    optional
Omitted selector lists fall back to the built-in heuristics.
Keys are domains, matched with and without a leading 'www.'. A malformed
entry is skipped with a warning naming only the domain; the rest still load.
This __comment key is ignored (it has no login_url).
